segment.source: ::The man greets you as soon as you enter his domain, smiling as he invites you further in with a wave of his hand. His smile, though, is forced, as a shroud of concern dims his eye's gleam and breaks the genuineness.::<end>

::An oily wrench lays on his desk, only an old smeared rag separating one from the other. You notice it, he notices it. An instant later, it disappears into one of his deep pockets, wrapped in the rag.::
That should not be there. We was, um... Gib and I were fixin' one of 'em two-oh-eights for a client of ours. Field repairs. Just got back to the shop, so sorry 'bout my appearance. So, ya here for a jet? Parts? Repairs?<end>
I'm interested in purchasing a jet ski.<end>

::You open your mouth, but the voice that is heard is not yours.::
I'm sorry: Name's Raymond Cerr, the owner. Eh, ya were sayin'...? <end>
::You notice that the previously quite observable anxiety has quickly dissipated. His smile broadens; his countenance brightens.::<end>
I'm looking for some spare components.<end>
Hardcore. Well, now, um, friend... ::He snaps his fingers.:: By the way, what do I call ya$(#, son/)? What's yer name?<end>
That is none of your business.<end>
::He raises his hands, chest height, palms facing forward.:: No need to act all hardcore, friend. I was just askin'. Imma just call ya... friend, then.<end>
Imma ask ya one thing now before we proceed: Is this your first jet or have you owned or at least ridden one before?<end>
Never owned, never ridden one before.<end>
So - a jet virgin. Pardon the expression. ::He laughs.:: That's o-kay, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName).<end>

We got lots of different jets, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName). The only question is whatcha need and how much coin ya got. If yer lookin' for somethin' cheaper, somethin' to getcha from point A to point B, we offer a variety of junk jets at yer disposal. If ya, however, wanna get from point A to point B mighty fast, maybe dominate some asshats along the way, or return to haulin' lots of loot - or just cruise around with style, then maybe ya oughta take a look at somethin' a bit better.<end>
I was thinking of something a bit cheaper.<end>
We'll find ya somethin' good, dontcha worry.<end>
Show me the good stuff. I'm not a zoner.<end>
Ha-ha, that's what I like to hear. <end>
Hardcore, hardcore. So ya got some experience. That's good, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName).<end>
I'm currently using some piece of junk, more like jetsam than jet, but now I'm itching to get the real deal.<end>

That is the rite of passage we must all take, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName). And it ain't just the coin, nah, ya can't just hop into a beast straight away, right? Ye'll dominate yerself if ya ain't got the experience. Can't deny that.<end>

we got a hardcore assortment of engines, batteries, suspensions - from cheap to coin-meltin', we got it all. Of course, we also stock cells for powerin' yer jets, ammo and all the-- Bah, enough of my yappin'. Lemme show ya what we got.<end>

Unless ya've suffered a breakdown, and by that I mean a malfunction which either prevents yer jet from operatin' at all, or impedes it so much ya can't drive it no more, there's no need for me to be takin' yer hard-earned coins for repairs ya could do on yer own.<end>

Instead, I could just sell ya one of our vehicle repair kits. They're cheap and so simple to use it is said if ya threw it in the water to them slackjaw fishes, they'd pick it right up and start fixin' stuff. ::He laughs.:: They can be used to perform all kinds of repairs on pretty much any type of vehicle under the stalactites, be it a jet, quad... heck, maybe even a powered frame like the Protectorate Dreadnought, I dunno. Ya just follow the instructions and yer hardcore.<end>
In that case, I'd like to purchase a few repair kits.<end>
I'll think about it. Let me ask you something else in the meantime.<end>
I'm interested in purchasing a jet ski.<end>
Sure, sure. Which one? Don't be afraid to ask questions, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName).<end>
Can I take a look at the expensive jet skis?<end>
Can I take a look at the cheap jet skis?<end>
I've decided which jet ski I want.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_torpedoFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0) stygian coins.::<end>
Congratulations, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName) - ya bought yerself a jet! <end>
Keep yer eyes on it real good. Them pirate sons of rats are everywhere now.<end>
And here's yer key. ::He hands you a jet ski key.::<end>
I'm sorry, but I can't accept that. I wish I could, I really wish, but ya know how dominatin' life is. Yeah?<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_blazerFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0) stygian coins.::<end>

::[Mercantile]:: $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_blazerFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0)? No way is it worth that much. I'll give you $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_blazerFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount3) for it.<end>
Actually, I think this might be too expensive for me. Mind if I choose another one?<end>
No need to rush, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName). Ya don't buy a jet every day. Just take yer time.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_phaserFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0) stygian coins.::<end>

::[Mercantile]:: $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_phaserFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0)? No way is it worth that much. I'll give you $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_phaserFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount3) for it.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_sharkFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0) stygian coins.::<end>

::[Mercantile]:: $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_sharkFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0)? No way is it worth that much. I'll give you $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_sharkFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount3) for it.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_glowFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0) stygian coins.::<end>
::[Mercantile]:: $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_glowFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0)? No way is it worth that much. I'll give you $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_glowFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount3) for it.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_plasmaLeviatorFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0) stygian coins.::<end>

::[Mercantile]:: $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_plasmaLeviatorFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0)? No way is it worth that much. I'll give you $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_plasmaLeviatorFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount3) for it.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_devastatorFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0) stygian coins.::<end>

Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_freighterFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0) stygian coins.::<end>

::[Mercantile]:: $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_freighterFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0)? No way is it worth that much. I'll give you $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_freighterFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount3) for it.<end>

::[Mercantile]:: $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_torpedoFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount0)? No way is it worth that much. I'll give you $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_torpedoFrame.BuyPriceWithDiscount3) for it.<end>
It's one of the junk jets.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him 600 stygian coins.::<end>
::[Mercantile]:: 600 seems a bit too much. How about 400?<end>
Sorry, that's too low. Even for a jet like this.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him 1100 stygian coins.::<end>
::[Mercantile]:: 1100 seems a bit too much. How about 800?<end>
Actually, it was that other one.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him 2700 stygian coins.::<end>
::[Mercantile]:: 2700 seems a bit too much. How about 2300?<end>
::[Mercantile]:: This thing isn't worth more than 1900 and you know it.<end>
Deal. Here's the money. ::Give him 3200 stygian coins.::<end>
::[Mercantile]:: 3200 seems a bit too much. How about 2800?<end>
::[Mercantile]:: This thing isn't worth more than 2400 and you know it.<end>
Actually, it's one of the expensive ones. My bad.<end>
I'd like to buy back that Reef Glider I sold you before.<end>

Sorry, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName), but I ain't sellin' that one to anyone. I've just grown to like it way too much. At first I was like, meh, it's odd and this and that, but now I absolutely love it - love it. And the performance - hardcore. Can't deny it, can't deny it.<end>
Ya should've thought about it real good before sellin' it to me.<end>

Speed. That's all there is to the Torpedo - speed. It's one of the finest examples of Hexagon engineering. It's twice as fast as a normal jet, twice as light, comes equipped with XG Turbopower 999 electric turbochargers which brings ya from naught to hardcore in the time it takes ya to press that sweet "turbo" button. It got two engines, baby, and almost no weight. This jet, this very jet, is *the* fastest jet in South Underrail. Let me repeat that: The *fastest* jet in South Underrail. Can't deny that.<end>

Speed. It comes at a price, though. And not just how much coin it's worth, but the fact that the frame offers little protection and durability, and that it handles best when yer goin' in a straight line.<end>
Speed, if that's all ya care about - get the Torpedo.<end>

This baby's a speeder. It's fast, light, reliable, has turbo - and it looks freakin' hardcore. My dad always used to tell me: "Son, if it got flames on it, it's badass." And so far he's been right. This is one *mean* machine, and it ain't a production machine. It's unique, one of a kind. Custom-built by skilled hands and a racer's heart.<end>

Didja know, back in the golden days of jet racin', before pirates started infestin' the waters and Protectorate started stickin' their nose everywhere, Mike Burnwater, the most hardcore jet racer that ever was used to dominate these waters. No one could touch him. He died, sadly, when his steerin' crapped out on him durin' a race around the Core Ring against the Great Jetso, his arch-nemesis, and he hit a wall and died in the explosion. This jet, the Blazer, was his brother's spare jet, but Mike himself did its flamin' paintjob.<end>
This is not just a machine - this baby got soul. Can't deny that.<end>

Another marvel from Hexagon. Even folks who don't like Hexagon aesthetics appreciate Phaser's mesmerizin' brilliance. There's somethin' hardcore about seein' a stream of lights shoot past ya in the dark, and that's what Phaser does best - movin' fast and lookin' stylish. Bein' the second-fastest jet I can offer ya, I think it's clear that this thing has a light frame, lotsa power and an electric turbocharger. Ya engage that and off ya go blindin' unsuspectin' folks.<end>

If ya want style and speed, this is the jet for ya. However, this ain't the jet ya wanna be bangin' about South Underrail. Most of the frame's been made from X1-class thermoplastic which reduces weight but makes the jet a lot less resistant to damage.<end>

The Shark is a jet with probably the oddest backstory I have in my shop. It's a custom-made jet that belonged to this vigilante from Junkyard, Gizzy McGold, who used to go huntin' for pirates before the Black Eels started suppressin' them. Stories say 'is wife had been zoned out by the pirates, which is why he went derailed and started killin' 'em.<end>

From what I know, it started out as yer typical junk jet, maybe an old SL model frame, but he put some decent armor on it, installed this triple rocket launcher - which uses Harp-1 rockets, and I got them for sale - good components... and then he went huntin'. Its speed is o-kay, but whatcha really want it for is its good armor and dominatin' firepower.<end>
Gizzy got zoned out a long time ago - not by pirates but by some teenage thug at The Rig - after which his jet went from hand to hand before it reached me.<end>

If Blazer's been made to speed in style, Glow's been made to zone out in style. Its whole frame has been made, or more specifically "additively manufactured," from the high-quality X3 thermoplastic which offers great durability and - due to the advantages of basically printin' a vehicle - a uniquely hardcore appearance. And o-kay speed, considerin' the weight of the frame.<end>

It comes with XL 55 twin lasers which draw power from the jet's primary battery. Ya gotta watch out not to use up all yer juice when shootin' those things.
The only real drawback this thing got is that it leaves ya a bit exposed. But other than that, it's one dominatin' jet. Can't deny that.<end>
Tell me about the Plasma Leviator.<end>

Glow's bigger brother. The Plasma Leviator is yet another hardcore jet hailin' from good ol' Hexagon. This thing is definitely not as stylish as Glow, but it packs a bigger punch without a question. Instead of lasers, this thing's got XP 39 twin plasma cannons which draw power from the jet's batteries. Yeah, it's got two, since this thing's a power hog.<end>
It's fairly slow due to its heavy armor and is the right choice for those who'd rather be tradin' speed for some extra protection and firepower.<end>

Devastator. The name says it all. Devastator. Manufactured by Biocorp Armory, Devastators were designed to be tanks on water and were to be used by the Underrail Protectorate. Equipped with a single state-of-the-art FC-2 fusion cannon, there isn't a vessel in this world short of a battleship that can come up against this ridable domination.<end>

However, it turns out the cost of makin' one of these, primarily because of the fusion cannon, was too high for Biocorp Armory to mass produce, especially once they figured out they rarely needed anythin' better than their old trusty Cruiser. Around ten of these have been made, and a few have been purchased by some dominatingly wealthy gentlemen in North Underrail. Eventually, one of those ended up here.<end>
What more can I say? It's slow even with two engines, it's devastatin', it has two batteries to last a long time... and it's the most expensive jet I got to offer.<end>

This jet is for those who got a lot of heavy baggage and a lot of time on their hands. The Biocorp Industries Freighter is a sturdy, affordable jet with two engines and two batteries, and o-kay protection. It's heavy and it's slow, but even with stock components it'll never struggle no matter how much stuff you've stuffed in it.<end>

Even though it isn't "designed" for towin', it can tow other jets no problem. Hell, I've used one of these many years ago to tow a small ferry, and I betcha can use it to even tow one of them fat rat yachts. And ya might find this surprisin', but it's one of the most comfortable and stable jets around, even when goin' at top speed. Can't deny that.<end>
What can you tell me about junk jets?<end>

The junk jets, as normal folks and pros alike tend to call 'em, are basically makeshift jets made from whatever's been lyin' around. They can come in many different shapes and sizes, but there are generally four frames which are used as bases for further modification. Twenty, thirty years ago, before the dissolution of Biocorp, there had been a large demand for jets, apparently. Since then a lot of those have been abandoned, damaged or disassembled, so folks have been takin' what they could find and started modifyin' them.<end>
The basic junk jet, the one that comes to everyone's mind when ya say "jet," is a small standin' jet. It's got o-kay speed, low durability, a simple trunk - but it gets the job done.<end>
Scrap jet is a more modern term for a larger standin' jet, 'cuz it got a bit more scrap on it. It's slightly heavier, but it offers more protection and durability.<end>

Then there's the "skimmer," which is the smaller kind of the sittin' jets, and the "scooter", the larger one. Sittin' jets are in general more durable but are slower.
What really makes the junk jets are their components. They might not be able to compete with the brand-name or higher-quality custom-built jets, but ya can tweak 'em and tune 'em to get somethin' really good for little coin.<end>
What are some important things I need to know when choosing a jet ski?<end>

Well, it depends on whatcha want from yer jet, but basically ya can break it down into four parts ya gotta consider: the frame - that's the most important one - the engine, the battery and the suspension. There's a bunch of stuff ya can get for yer jet, accessories and what not, but these four are the pipes and barrels.<end>

The frame is the jet itself. Ya can exchange engines and batteries - with limitations, of course - and tune yer jet to yer likin', but ya change the frame and it ain't the same jet no more. Ya want a speeder? Ya get a light, slick, sexy frame. Ya want a fighter? Ya want it to be sturdy, to have guns and armor. Ya wanna haul loot? Room for a big engine so ya got a lotta power.<end>

Speakin' of that, weight of the frame is a very important thing, 'cuz no matter how hardcore yer engine is, if that thing's too heavy, ya ain't gonna be doin' any racin' with it. Some frames can support certain components which others cannot, and some can even support multiple engines and batteries. So ya gotta be thinkin' about that as well if ya wanna upgrade yer jet.<end>

The engine is what makes yer jet move. Now, before I continue, I work with electrics only. I say that 'cuz there are ass-joes out there that do build jets - and vehicles in general - that got internal combustion engines. Yeah, yeah. Mhm. People use what people got layin' about, eh?<end>

Anyways, when it comes to engines, things are fairly straightforward, especially nowadays when everythin' so modular. By the way, some jets can support *two* engines, so ya just connect the extra one and now ya got two. Easy-peasy. <end>

The better the engine is, the more power yer jet's gonna have and the faster it's gonna go. Ya got some limitations on the size of the engine ya can put in a jet, of course, which mostly depends on its frame, and some engines use more juice than others relative to their output. Other than that, though, it's just a matter of cashin' it out and puttin' it in, and that's somethin' even a zoner can do. If he had the coins...<end>

A jet ain't gonna run on love and carin' - it needs juice. The battery's what provides that very juice. Pretty much all jet batteries got the same voltage, so they are interchangeable, therefore the differences between batteries lie primarily in their size and their capacity. <end>

The higher the capacity, the longer ya can drive yer jet before needin' to recharge it. If ya can't fit a battery in yer frame, ya better choose a smaller battery. And that's it, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName). That's all ya gotta know about jet batteries.<end>

The suspension is what keeps yer jet stable and easier to control. Technically, ya can do without it, but let's face it - life's a lot better if ya got it. Water is an uneven surface, where even when there aren't any waves yer still ridin' on somethin' that's providin' a lot of resistance.<end>

Suspension helps ya improve yer ride quality, keep yer aim steadier and makes yer landin' much better when yer bouncin' over them waves at a hundred kilometers an hour. The most important thing is to make sure the size of the suspension is right for the jet. Everythin' else is just a matter of how much coin ya want to exchange for stability.<end>
Got it. Let's talk about jet skis.<end>
There was something else I wanted to ask you.<end>
Can I take a closer look at the jet skis?<end>
Sure, sure. Inspect any jet ya like. And feel free to take a look at what's under the hood, heh. If ya got questions, just ask.<end>
I'll go take a closer look at the jet skis.<end>
I'll be around if ya need anythin'.<end>
I'd like to take a look at some of the jet skis you have available.<end>
Is that all you got in your inventory, Ray? I expected a better selection from the only jet ski shop in South Underrail.<end>
I can't say whether I have somethin' hardcore lyin' in the back, but I can say that if I did, it would be for special customers only.<end>
::[Mercantile]:: If being one of your special customers means having more money than self-control, then I might just be that kind of person.<end>
Eh, I can't reveal what makes one a special customer, but ya certainly got it. Check this out.<end>
Ya don't look the part, $(context.npc_cc_ray_playerName). Yeah-- I mean I ain't sayin' that's what makes a special customer in the first place, no.<end>
I see. I'm interested in something else, then.<end>
I'd like to sell a jet to you.<end>
So ya know, I ain't interested in buyin' no junk jets - ya know, the makeshift ones. I'm interested in quality jets only. If that's whatcha got, just <end>
bring yer jet inside and we'll take a look at 'er. There're buttons by the jet lift ya can use to raise and lower the gate.<end>
How much will you give me for the Torpedo?<end>
I ain't buyin' it without the key, just so ya know. If ya got the key, and ya agree to the price, then we got ourselves a deal.<end>
We got ourselves a deal. ::Sell the Torpedo for $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_torpedoFrame.SellPriceWithIncrease0).::<end>
Oh, and if ya think ya might've forgotten somethin' in yer jet, check that gray locker in the corner of my office. I put everythin' I find there. Okay?<end>
::He sighs.:: Ya drive a hard bargain. O-kay, <end>
We got ourselves a deal. ::Sell the Blazer for $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_blazerFrame.SellPriceWithIncrease0).::<end>
::He sighs.:: Ya drive a hard bargain. O-kay, <end>
::[Mercantile]:: Come on, Ray, you can do better than that. How about $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_blazerFrame.SellPriceWithIncrease2)? We got a deal?<end>
::[Mercantile]:: What the hell, Ray? I got a guy offerin' me $(context.VehicleStatus_xpbl_blazerFrame.SellPriceWithIncrease3) and I'm wasting my time here with you.<end>
Then how are ya ridin'-- Never mind.<end>
I need to think about this some more.<end>
As long as ya'd like. I ain't goin' nowhere. Not unless I get an emergency call.<end>
No. Sorry, I can't accept that.<end>
I'm sorry, but that's my offer.<end>

How much will you give me for the Plasma Leviator?<end>
How much will you give me for the Devastator?<end>
How much will you give me for the Freighter?<end>
How much will you give me for the Protectorate Cruiser?<end>

Whoa, whoa, hold down a second here. I can't just purchase some random military or, or law enforcement jets. These things can get a man in a lotta trouble, especially if their background ain't as clear as it should be.<end>
It's not like you don't sell military jets already.<end>
I got the Devastator fair and square, with proper papers and all, and no one ever bothered me about it. Still, I ain't flauntin' it around just in case. But this? No. Sorry.<end>
I don't want someone knockin' on my door and askin' questions.<end>
How much will you give me for the Aegis Patroller?<end>
I'd like to sell you a Reef Glider.<end>
What kind of a jet is it?<end>
It's a very old type of jet ski, a relic, one can say. It was manufactured by NFT more than two centuries ago and the chances of finding a functional one are as slim as a zoner's wallet.<end>
How much ya askin' for it?<end>
Hardcore. Ooh, and it's a nice-looking key too.<end>
Oh, Imma enjoy takin' this baby out for its first ride, *mhm*. Soon as I close the shop, he-he.<end>
No. The key has been lost a long time ago, sadly.<end>

::He frowns sligthly.::
I usually don't buy 'em without keys, but this... this is too hardcore to pass on. O-kay. I'm o-kay without the key.<end>
I need to think about this.<end>
Frankly, I have no clue myself.<end>
Don't worry, no one will be coming to collect this jet ski.<end>
Uh, that can have many different meanings...<end>
Never heard of a Reef Glider?<end>
